- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.20), model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk-off bias.  
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast 2–3 days post-spike.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is > 2σ above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings (e.g., +0.17, -0.22, +0.11), model tends to lag by 1–2 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight downward bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 65.00, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 30d window.
